Subject: Follow-up: cryptographic key model options & SOC 2 evidence pack for CardioHealth

Hi Ellen —

Thanks for taking the time today — really appreciated the deep dive into CardioHealth's encryption and evidence needs. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the options we discussed and propose next steps so your security team can evaluate without having to rehash details.

Quick recap of what CardioHealth asked about:
- Current SOC 2 posture and what evidence we can share (scope, Type I/II cadence)
- Encryption in transit and at rest details, including algorithms and rotation windows
- Customer-managed key options (BYOK) vs. Redwood-managed keys, and HSM-backed CMKs
- Audit/logging for key operations and exportable proofs for audits

Attached: Redwood_SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf and Redwood_KMS_Model_Options.xlsx — the latter outlines three deployment patterns (Redwood-managed KMS, Customer BYOK using cloud KMS, and HSM-backed CMK with external HSM vendor).

Recommended next steps (proposed timeline):
1) You and Tom to review the attached KMS model matrix by Mon 05/24 — mark any must-have requirements.
2) I’ll schedule a focused security intake with Aditya (runtime engineer) and Monica (security ops) — 45 minutes to walk through logging/export and HSM integration details. Suggested slot: Tue 05/25 10:00–10:45 PT.
3) If BYOK/HSM is a blocker, we can prepare a short PoC plan (2–3 weeks) to validate the key import flow and KMS rotation hooks.

A couple of clarifications from our side that may help your evaluation:
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a Type II report with a rolling 12-month scope; the summary has the on-scope controls. For full reports we require an NDA + secure transfer; the summary PDF includes the roster of controls and auditor contact.
- HSM: We support HSM-wrapped keys (external HSM via customer-provided connector) and cloud-KMS CMKs (AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault/GCP KMS). For FIPS 140-2/3 requirements we recommend the HSM-backed CMK path.
- Key rotation: automated rotation is supported; rotation windows and grace periods are configurable per-customer.

Action: please reply with the best people on your side for the intake (if different than Tom/Security) and whether Tue 05/25 10:00 PT works.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim

Thanks Rachel — useful recap. A few immediate clarifying questions from our security team:

1) For the HSM-backed CMK option, are you able to support an external HSM vendor (we're evaluating Thales and Entrust) and hold the key envelope so that Redwood never sees unwrapped key material? We need to confirm you do not persist plaintext keys in your control plane.

2) Audit logs: can you provide an exportable, timestamped log of all key-related operations (import, wrap/unwrap, rotate, access attempts) for at least 2 years? We may need to ingest those into our SIEM.

3) SOC 2 report: we will sign an NDA for the full report — please confirm the transfer mechanism (SFTP/secure Drive) and any redactions you apply. Also, is the report within the last 12 months?

4) HIPAA question: CardioHealth is a covered entity — do you have a standard BAA? If not, can Redwood provide the necessary commitments to handle PHI and support our HIPAA controls?

Tom and I are available for the intake; Tue 05/25 10:00 PT works for us.

- Ellen
Ellen Park
Director, Information Security
CardioHealth
ellen.park@cardiohealth.io

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. I’ll address each item and we can use the intake to show examples.

1) External HSM vendors: yes — we support importing keys that are wrapped by customer HSMs and can accept the key envelope such that Redwood never handles unwrapped key material. For Thales/Entrust specifically, our connector supports PKCS#11/Wrapping workflows. We will document the vendor-specific steps in the intake.

2) Audit logs: we provide key-operation events streamed to a customer-owned S3/Blob storage (or pushed to your SIEM via secure Syslog/HTTPS). The retention and exportable formats (JSON/CSV) are configurable; we can demonstrate a sample export during the intake. Our default retention for key ops is 24 months for enterprise tenants.

3) SOC 2: the report is a Type II and was issued within the last 9 months. For the full report transfer we use an NDA + secure SFTP/bg-encrypted Drive (DocuSign + secure transfer link). Rachel will send the NDA template and the secure transfer link. We do not redact control IDs, only any customer-identifying data if requested.

4) BAA/HIPAA: Redwood has a standard BAA for customers handling PHI; legal typically adds a few operational clauses for key material control. We can share our BAA in the intake packet.

During the intake I can walk the team through a short demo of the import/unwrap flow, show a sample log export, and review the PoC checklist if you want to accelerate to HSM verification.

See you Tue 05/25 10:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Regards,
